Financial ML Tuning and Model Selection¶

This notebook performs focused second-round hyperparameter tuning for the supervised PaySim V1 fraud detection models:

  1. Logistic Regression
  2. Random Forest
  3. XGBoost

The goal is to tune candidate supervised model families and select the final supervised ML model using validation performance only. The test set is not used for model selection.

Important: This notebook does not implement Autoencoder anomaly detection, risk scoring, Streamlit, API, or Docker.

1. Import Libraries and Project Functions¶

Most reusable logic comes from src/, including preprocessing, model pipelines, tuning utilities, and evaluation helpers.

Data Preparation Strategy¶

This notebook reuses the same preprocessing, train/validation/test split, and training-only sampling strategy as notebook 02. The steps are repeated here so notebook 03 can run independently and so tuned model results are comparable to the baseline results.

3. Feature Engineering¶

We reuse the same engineered features from the baseline notebook. The target column isFraud, ID-like columns nameOrig and nameDest, and rule-based isFlaggedFraud are excluded from model features by default.

4. Train / Validation / Test Split¶

The split logic matches notebook 02:

  • X_train_full / y_train_full: original full training split before sampling
  • X_val / y_val: untouched validation set for tuned model comparison
  • X_test / y_test: untouched holdout test set
  • validation is used for model tuning comparison
  • the test set is not used for model selection
In [58]:

5. Sample Training Data Only¶

X_train_full and y_train_full are the original full training split before sampling. To keep local tuning runnable, sampling is applied only to this training split. The sampled result is named X_train_sampled and y_train_sampled. Validation and test sets are not sampled.

6. Build Candidate Model Pipelines and Tuning Spaces¶

We reuse the same model families from notebook 02, then define focused second-round parameter search spaces using pipeline parameter names such as model__max_depth and model__learning_rate. Logistic Regression is retained mainly as an interpretable baseline. Random Forest is searched around its current best region. XGBoost tuning focuses on reducing false positives by testing lower scale_pos_weight values and slightly more conservative parameter ranges.

In [62]:
numeric_features, categorical_features = get_feature_columns()

candidate_models = get_baseline_models(
    numeric_features,
    categorical_features,
    y_train_sampled=y_train_sampled,
    random_state=RANDOM_STATE,
)

param_distributions = get_tuning_param_distributions(y_train_sampled=y_train_sampled)

print("Candidate models:")
print(list(candidate_models.keys()))

7. Tune Candidate Models¶

The tuning uses a focused second-round randomized search:

  • n_iter=20
  • cv=5
  • scoring="average_precision"

cv=5 gives a more stable cross-validation estimate than cv=3. n_iter=20 explores more parameter combinations while still keeping runtime manageable. The search now focuses on the strongest observed regions instead of broad exploration.

In [63]:
tuned_searches = tune_candidate_models(
    models=candidate_models,
    param_distributions=param_distributions,
    X_train=X_train_sampled,
    y_train=y_train_sampled,
    scoring="average_precision",
    cv=5,
    n_iter=20,
    random_state=RANDOM_STATE,
)

Hyperparameter Search Diagnostics¶

This section visualizes the RandomizedSearchCV results from the fitted tuning searches. The goal is to inspect how cross-validation average precision changes across tested hyperparameter values and to check whether the current candidate ranges appear reasonable. Because this notebook uses focused second-round tuning with n_iter=20 and cv=5, these plots help inspect whether the narrowed candidate ranges are behaving reasonably, while still not being an exhaustive hyperparameter analysis.

Build Combined Search Results DataFrame¶

The fitted tuned_searches object already contains cross-validation results for each model. We convert those results into one combined table for inspection and saving.

In [64]:
def get_search_results_df(tuned_searches):
    rows = []

    for model_name, search in tuned_searches.items():
        results = pd.DataFrame(search.cv_results_).copy()
        results["model"] = model_name

        keep_columns = [
            "model",
            "mean_test_score",
            "std_test_score",
            "rank_test_score",
            "params",
        ]
        keep_columns += [col for col in results.columns if col.startswith("param_")]
        rows.append(results[keep_columns])

    return pd.concat(rows, axis=0, ignore_index=True)


search_results_df = get_search_results_df(tuned_searches)
search_results_sorted = search_results_df.sort_values(["model", "rank_test_score"])

Hyperparameter Value vs CV Score¶

These plots summarize the average CV score observed for each tested parameter value. Since this is randomized focused tuning, each value may still appear only a limited number of times.

In [67]:
def plot_param_vs_score(search_results_df, model_name, param_col):
    model_results = search_results_df[search_results_df["model"] == model_name].copy()

    if param_col not in model_results.columns:
        print(f"{param_col} is not available for {model_name}. Skipping.")
        return

    model_results[param_col] = model_results[param_col].astype(str)
    plot_data = model_results.groupby(param_col)["mean_test_score"].mean()

    plt.figure(figsize=(7, 4))
    plt.plot(plot_data.index, plot_data.values, marker="o")
    plt.title(f"{model_name}: {param_col} vs CV Average Precision")
    plt.xlabel(param_col)
    plt.ylabel("Mean CV Average Precision")
    plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha="right")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

Boundary Check Summary¶

This check helps decide whether future tuning should expand candidate ranges. Boundary results are only diagnostic and do not change the current notebook selection logic.

In [71]:
def check_best_params_on_boundary(tuned_searches, param_distributions):
    for model_name, search in tuned_searches.items():
        print(f"\n{model_name}")
        best_params = search.best_params_
        search_space = param_distributions.get(model_name, {})

        for param_name, best_value in best_params.items():
            candidates = search_space.get(param_name)

            if candidates is None:
                print(f"- {param_name}: {best_value} (not found in search space)")
                continue

            numeric_candidates = [value for value in candidates if isinstance(value, (int, float)) and value is not None]
            is_ordered_numeric = len(numeric_candidates) == len(candidates) and len(numeric_candidates) > 1

            if not is_ordered_numeric:
                print(f"- {param_name}: {best_value} (categorical / not ordered)")
                continue

            lower = min(numeric_candidates)
            upper = max(numeric_candidates)

            if best_value == lower:
                print(f"- {param_name}: {best_value} is at the lower tested boundary; future tuning could try lower values.")
            elif best_value == upper:
                print(f"- {param_name}: {best_value} is at the upper tested boundary; future tuning could try higher values.")
            else:
                print(f"- {param_name}: {best_value} is inside the candidate range; the current range appears reasonable for this focused tuning stage.")


check_best_params_on_boundary(tuned_searches, param_distributions)

Final Supervised Model Refit and Holdout Evaluation¶

The final supervised model is selected using validation performance after tuning. After selection, we refit that selected tuned pipeline using train + validation data only. The test set remains untouched until the final holdout evaluation.

This refitted model is saved for later integration with the Autoencoder and risk scoring modules. It is the final supervised ML model, not the final integrated risk system.

Combine Train and Validation Data¶

We combine the original full training split (X_train_full, y_train_full) with the untouched validation set (X_val, y_val). Then we apply training-only sampling again to the combined train + validation data. The test set is not included.

We clone the selected best estimator before refitting. This creates a fresh pipeline with the same best hyperparameters, then fits it on the sampled train + validation data.

10. Final Notes¶

  • Hyperparameter tuning used a focused second-round randomized search with n_iter=20 and cv=5.
  • The validation set was used for tuned model comparison and final supervised model selection.
  • The final refit used train + validation data only.
  • The test set was used only once at the end for holdout evaluation.
  • The refitted supervised model is saved for later integration with Autoencoder and risk scoring modules.
  • This model is the final supervised ML model, not the final integrated risk system.
  • This PaySim V1 system remains a post-transaction fraud detection and risk monitoring system because it uses balance-related fields such as newbalanceOrig and newbalanceDest.

Next Step¶

Build the Autoencoder anomaly detection module in 04_financial_autoencoder_experiment.ipynb as a supplementary risk signal. Integrated risk scoring will be developed later in 05_financial_risk_scoring_and_dashboard_prep.ipynb after both supervised ML and Autoencoder signals are available.
